samples.summary: `OfflineRuntime` is mounted unconditionally, so every signed-in session pays for a feature nobody can enable
samples.evidence: `PrivateRoute` renders `<OfflineRuntime userId={String(me.id)} />` with no gate on `supportsClientKey()`, on `getOfflinePersistenceEnabled()`, or on anything being stored. Its effect (offline-runtime.tsx) unconditionally constructs a `WafflebaseDocStore` (opening/creating the `wafflebase-offline` IndexedDB database), runs `collectStale()`, and awaits `fetchDocuments()` — an extra, un-react-query-cached, unfiltered document listing — before `purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments`. At the pinned `@yorkie-js/react@0.7.22` nothing can ever be written to that store (`supportsClientKey()` is false), and even after the bump the preference is off by default. The design states the opposite property in § Turning it on: "Users who never opt in pay nothing for this feature existing." The reconcile and sweep are only meaningful once something has been stored, and both the preference and the capability are synchronous checks available at mount, so the early-out is cheap. Cost as shipped: one extra API round trip and one IndexedDB database per session for 100% of users while 0% can benefit.

samples.summary: None of the design's Goals are delivered on this branch: the durable path is gated above the pinned dependency
samples.evidence: `supportsClientKey()` compares the injected `__YORKIE_REACT_VERSION__` against `MinClientKeyVersion = "0.7.23"`, and `packages/frontend/package.json` pins `"@yorkie-js/react": "0.7.22"` (line 66). With the gate closed, `useDurableDocument` refuses every document, no `DurableYorkieProvider` mounts, no store is ever attached, the `saved-locally` chip state is unreachable, and both opt-in entry points (Settings section, chip offer) are hidden. So Goal 1 — "Edits made while disconnected survive a reload or a browser crash" — is not satisfied by anything in this diff. The design acknowledges this (§ Rollout: "PR 4 lands inert... the Goals at the top of this document are unmet until the dependency is bumped"), so it is deliberate rather than an oversight, but it means the change ships ~4,000 lines of subsystem whose only integration with a real durable client is exercised by tests that stub `supportsClientKey` to true. Flagging so the tradeoff is weighed explicitly rather than inherited: the reviewable behavior arrives with a later one-line dependency bump that will touch no code here.

samples.summary: `deleteWorkspace` always makes two extra API calls for offline cleanup, unlike `removeMember`, which gates on `isOfflineUser`
samples.evidence: `deleteWorkspace` calls `await documentIdsIn(id)` unconditionally (line 127); `documentIdsIn` issues `fetchWorkspace(ref)` and `fetchDocuments()` (lines 103-104). `removeMember` twelve lines below does gate the identical call: `const doomed = leaving ? await documentIdsIn(workspaceId) : []` (line 160), where `leaving = isOfflineUser(String(userId))`. `purgeOfflineDocuments` no-ops when there is no offline user, but that check happens *after* the two round trips. The result is two extra requests on every workspace deletion for every user, including those who never enabled offline persistence and those on the current pin where nothing can be stored — the same "pay nothing" property the design asserts. An `isOfflineUser`-style early-out (or a `getOfflinePersistenceEnabled()` check) would make the two call sites consistent.

samples.summary: Design doc says recovery reuses `DocumentCopyService` / `POST /documents/:id/copy`; the implementation uses the import path instead
samples.evidence: § Losing work anyway: "we already have the machinery for it in `DocumentCopyService` / `POST /documents/:id/copy`", and See Also (line 648) lists document-copy.md as "the copy engine the offline-copy recovery path reuses". `offline-copy-recovery.ts` uses neither: it calls `createWorkspaceDocument()` then `applyImportedContent()` (the Miro/file-import writer), plus a bespoke `writeNote()` that spins up its own Yorkie `Client`. The implementation choice looks correct — `POST /documents/:id/copy` duplicates a document the *server* holds, which by construction cannot carry offline-only edits, and one of the three archive causes is the source being deleted upstream — so the doc is what is wrong. Left as-is, the canonical doc points a future reader at a reuse relationship that does not exist and hides the real one (`apply-imported-content.ts`).

samples.summary: The doc's own four-PR rollout ("land separately, so that a regression in either is unambiguous") is landed as one change
samples.evidence: § Rollout tables PR 2 (`WafflebaseDocStore`, "not yet wired"), PR 3 (per-document client + app lock, "still passing no store"), PR 4 (wire the store, Settings/chip opt-in, `durable` chip, recovery) and PR 5 (revise `sync-status.md`). This diff contains all four: the store and its four test files, `durable-session.ts`/`use-durable-document.ts`, `durable-yorkie-provider.tsx` + `offline-runtime.tsx` + the Settings section + the chip states, and the `sync-status.md` revision. The task plan confirms it (`20260917-offline-wiring-todo.md` Task 8 adds the PR-4 wiring into the same branch as Tasks 1-7). The stated benefit of the split — attributing a regression to the structural half or the behavioral half — is forfeited. Cost is process-only, and is partly mitigated by the version gate keeping the behavioral half dark.

samples.summary: `keepArchives` is a dead option whose rationale names a caller the design says must not exist
samples.evidence: `dropAllForUser(userId, { keepArchives })` (line 1123) and `eraseOfflineData(store, userId, { keepArchives })` (offline-erase.ts:30) both accept the flag, and the comment at wafflebase-doc-store.ts:1154 justifies it as "for the one caller that did not ask for any of this: a session the server expired." No caller in the repo passes it: grep for `keepArchives` across `packages/frontend/**/*.ts` returns only the two declarations and the one `if (!options.keepArchives)`. That is because the design settled the opposite way — the 401 arm erases *nothing at all* (`eraseLocalData: "none"` in `fetchWithAuth`, and the cleanup table row "Session expired (401) | Nothing"). So this is a leftover from an earlier iteration of the design, carrying a comment that contradicts the shipped one. knip will not catch it (it is an option property, not an export).

samples.summary: The doc specifies an `onupgradeneeded` migration of existing store entries; the code ships v1 with no migration and says none is needed
samples.evidence: § Storage, Layout and migration: "An `onupgradeneeded` that relocates each existing value into the snapshot store, with an empty change log beside it, is the whole migration." `wafflebase-doc-store.ts` sets `DB_VERSION = 1` and its upgrade handler comments "Version 1 creates; there is nothing in the wild to migrate. No wafflebase build has ever passed `ClientOptions.store`, so no browser holds an older layout." The code's reasoning is sound and the doc paragraph is stale — but as the canonical subsystem doc it now describes a migration path that does not exist, which is the kind of divergence the next person extending the schema will trust.

samples.summary: The docKey type↔prefix convention is duplicated again rather than extracted
samples.evidence: `TYPE_PREFIXES` in offline-copy-recovery.ts is a prefix→type table that inverts `buildDocKey()` in `app/documents/apply-imported-content.ts` (type→prefix, lines 37-48), which the same recovery flow already imports for `applyImportedContent`. Two more encodings of the same convention arrive in this change: `isExcluded(docKey) => docKey.startsWith("pdf-")` in `lib/use-durable-document.ts`, and `isDocument()` / `documentKeyOf()` in `wafflebase-doc-store.ts`. The scatter predates this change (each detail route inlines its own `` `sheet-${id}` `` literal), but the change extends it by three sites in `lib/` without extracting a shared helper — and `TYPE_PREFIXES` additionally has to carry `note-`, which `buildDocKey` does not know about, so the two tables are already inconsistent with each other. Risk is divergence when a sixth CRDT type is added: the editor route, the import writer, and the recovery reader would each need updating independently.

samples.summary: Note recovery reimplements `applyImportedContent`'s client lifecycle instead of adding a `note` arm to it
samples.evidence: `writeNote()` constructs its own `Client`, activates, attaches a `Document<{content?: Text}>` on `note-${docId}`, edits, detaches and deactivates — the same activate/attach/write/detach/deactivate shape `applyImportedContent` already implements for four types, including the same "activate outside the try" comment copied across. Its own doc comment explains why (`ImportedContent` has no note variant because a note is one Yorkie `Text` rather than an engine document), which is a fair reason to skip the *content* branch but not a reason to duplicate the *lifecycle*. The repo's stated preference is reuse; extending `ImportedContent` with a `{ type: "note"; markdown: string }` arm would have kept one copy of the client handling and one place to fix an attach/detach bug.

samples.summary: The Miro import module's handle semantics are widened to serve offline recovery
samples.evidence: `MappedInit` now accepts `id` alongside `__id`, `handleOf()` falls back to `element.id`, and the new `mapDescendants()` registers group children in the handle map. These exist for the recovery path (the doc comment says so explicitly), but they change behavior for the Miro import path too: any mapped element that happens to carry an `id` now gets registered as a connector target, where before only `__id` did. Reusing the module is the right call over forking it; the widening is just worth naming as a shared-module semantic change made on behalf of a different caller.

samples.summary: IndexedDB open/transaction plumbing and byte-budget eviction already exist in `packages/debug-report/src/store.ts`
samples.evidence: `debug-report`'s `indexedDbBlobs()` (store.ts:161) carries its own `indexedDB.open` + `onupgradeneeded` + transaction-settle plumbing and a `DEFAULT_BUDGET_BYTES` eviction policy, and the frontend already depends on `@wafflebase/debug-report`. The new store reimplements `open()`, `requested()`, `completed()` and an eviction policy from scratch. The shapes genuinely differ (compound keys, four object stores, per-user indexes, quota-retry) so full reuse was never on the table — noting only that the lowest layer of plumbing had a precedent, and neither module is factored to share it.

samples.summary: Reversed Non-Goals are kept as struck-through text plus an annotation rather than rewritten
samples.evidence: `sync-status.md`'s Non-Goals now read "~~**Offline persistence.**~~ **No longer a Non-Goal**" and "~~**A user-facing offline mode toggle.**~~ Shipped as...". CONTRIBUTING asks that an area's doc be updated rather than paralleled, which this does — but a Non-Goals section that lists two things that are now goals, struck through, states the old and new positions at once and leaves the reader to work out which is current. Rewriting the entries (with the history in the linked offline doc, which already carries it) would read cleaner. Taste, not a rule.

verdict.reason: The claimed code is present exactly as described. PrivateRoute.tsx:35 renders <OfflineRuntime userId={String(me.id)} /> with no gate on supportsClientKey(), getOfflinePersistenceEnabled(), or anything being stored (whole file, lines 1-45, contains no such check). offline-runtime.tsx:63-198 likewise has no guard in its effect: it constructs a WafflebaseDocStore at :89, calls store.collectStale() at :123 (which reaches open() -> indexedDB.open("wafflebase-offline") at wafflebase-doc-store.ts:456-459, DEFAULT_DB_NAME at :35, so the database is created lazily but unconditionally per session), and awaits an uncached fetchDocuments() at :155 before purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments. Only retryPendingOfflineErase short-circuits cheaply (offline-erase.ts:360-364). Both suggested gates exist and are used as gates elsewhere in the same feature (settings/page.tsx:35, collab-document-provider.tsx:223, use-durable-document.ts:128, durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:186), so they were available and synchronous. The design property quoted is real (docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md:164-165 "Users who never opt in pay nothing for this feature existing"), and the task doc confirms nothing can be written at the pinned @yorkie-js/react 0.7.22 (docs/tasks/active/20260917-offline-wiring-todo.md:242-246). No refutation ground applies: not not-present (code is verbatim as claimed); not already-guarded (private-route.test.tsx:64-74 asserts unconditional mounting, and no caller-side gate exists); not out-of-scope, because the cost — one extra API round trip and one IndexedDB database per signed-in session for every user while none can benefit at the pin — falls outside mere codebase tidiness. I note there are real design counter-arguments for running some housekeeping ungated (the cross-account 30-day sweep at design :314-321, and finishing an owed erase at :224), which bears on the right remedy, but it does not make the finding not-real or unreachable.

verdict.reason: Every factual element of the finding checks out in the tree. `MinClientKeyVersion = "0.7.23"` (packages/frontend/src/lib/yorkie-capabilities.ts:24) is compared against the build-injected `@yorkie-js/react` pin (vite.config.ts:414), which package.json:66 sets to "0.7.22"; `atLeast` therefore returns false and `supportsClientKey()` is false for any real build of this branch. That gate sits upstream of every durable surface: the persistence decision (collab-document-provider.tsx:223, use-durable-document.ts:128), the Settings opt-in section (app/settings/page.tsx:35,111 wraps the entire Offline section in `{offlineAvailable && …}`), and the chip's offer (sync-status-chip.tsx:97). So no durable client mounts, no store is attached, and the `saved-locally` state is unreachable outside tests that stub the capability true (collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx:134, use-durable-document.test.tsx:36, sync-status-chip.test.tsx:495, settings-offline.test.tsx:11-34). The design doc's own Goals (offline-local-persistence.md:45-57) are consequently undelivered, which the doc concedes at :612-622. No refutation ground applies: the code is present exactly as described, no caller guard makes it moot, and spec conformance to the design's stated outcome is squarely this lens. The tradeoff being deliberate and documented is an argument about severity that a maintainer should weigh; I cannot read the originating issue's acceptance criteria, so I cannot establish that shipping with the Goals unmet was accepted, and uncertainty keeps the finding.

finding.summary: The "dark launch" is not one: on the shipped 0.7.22 pin every document publishes the `unsupported` lapse, so every user's `Not saved` tooltip now blames their browser for our dependency pin
finding.evidence:
`packages/frontend/package.json:66` pins `@yorkie-js/react` to `0.7.22`, and `yorkie-capabilities.ts` sets `MinClientKeyVersion = "0.7.23"`, so `supportsClientKey()` is false for every render today. The lapse is computed at `collab-document-provider.tsx:291-299` as `decided?.durable ? undefined : !supportsClientKey() ? "unsupported" : …`, and `DurabilityLapseScope` wraps BOTH branches (lines ~340+), i.e. it is published for every collaborative document, durable or not. `sync-status-tooltip.ts` LAPSE_REASONS maps `unsupported` → "This browser cannot save documents locally." and `tooltipFor`'s `not-saved` arm appends it unconditionally (`const why_not = lapse ? ...`).

Net effect on the current pin: 100% of users — nobody has opted in, nobody can — who go offline with unsent edits see a tooltip asserting a false thing about their browser. The design's Rollout section stakes the whole staging argument on "nothing changes for anyone until they opt in" (offline-local-persistence.md § Rollout), and sync-status.md's central risk is "the chip could imply durability it does not have" — this is the mirror of that risk: the chip now mis-attributes the absence of durability. Either gate the lapse scope on the feature being reachable, or give the version-pin case wording that does not accuse the user's browser.

verdict.reason: Every element of the claim checks out against the tree. package.json:66 pins @yorkie-js/react to 0.7.22; vite.config.ts:414-418 injects that pin as __YORKIE_REACT_VERSION__; yorkie-capabilities.ts:24,44-82 makes supportsClientKey() false for that pin. collab-document-provider.tsx:291-299 computes the lapse with `!supportsClientKey() ? "unsupported"` as the FIRST branch, so it wins over not-permitted/not-enabled on every route, and it can never be short-circuited by `decided?.durable` because use-durable-document.ts:127-132 gates eligibility on the same capability (settling immediately at line 254). DurabilityLapseScope at collab-document-provider.tsx:350 wraps BOTH branches, so the value is published for every collaborative document. sync-status-chip.tsx:79,322 reads and forwards it unconditionally, and sync-status-tooltip.ts:111-112 appends LAPSE_REASONS[lapse] in the not-saved arm with no gate — line 30 being 'This browser cannot save documents locally.' Notably the chip's sibling consumer offerOffline (sync-status-chip.tsx:95-99) IS gated on supportsClientKey(), so the offer is suppressed on this pin while the accusatory sentence is not; there is no guard making the lapse path unreachable. The design conflict is documented: docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md:520 assigns that exact sentence to 'IndexedDB unavailable (private browsing)', not to a version pin, and lines 597-599 stake the dark launch on 'nothing changes for anyone until they opt in' while lines 226-230 require the capability gate on every user-facing surface, not only the persisting code. Under the design-fit rubric this is spec-conformance (an acceptance/outcome criterion left unmet with a user-visible cost: 100% of users on the current pin are told a false thing about their browser when offline with unsent edits), not a line-level correctness nit, so it stays in lane and is major. No refutation ground applies.
